study.technique_notes: Six levels of one acquisition, confirmed by the user. No burned-in annotation, callipers, scale bar, or HU ROI on any frame, so nothing here is quantitatively anchored. Bulky soft tissue at both lateral field margins is consistent with shoulder girdle / proximal arms within the scan field.

frames.slice_level: Upper thorax, at or just above the aortic arch (approximately T2-T4). Trachea round and midline; no arch contour resolved.
frames.notes: First frame supplied. Pixels not attached — arrived as a conversation attachment rather than a file.

frames.slice_level: Carina / proximal main bronchi, approximately T5-T6. Airway seen centrally as a transverse lucency at the bifurcation.
frames.notes: Second frame supplied, caudal to the first. Hilar vascular branching well seen bilaterally at this level. Pixels not attached.

frames.slice_level: Below the carina, at the main bronchi / bronchus intermedius, approximately T6-T7. Both bronchi visible as paired lucencies within the mediastinum.
frames.notes: Third frame supplied, caudal to the carinal frame. Largest lung cross-section of the three, with pulmonary vessels radiating prominently from both hila as expected at this level. Broad homogeneous central mediastinal soft tissue corresponds to heart and great vessels, undifferentiated because the study is unenhanced. Pixels not attached.

frames.slice_level: Lower thorax at heart level, approximately T7-T8. Heart occupies most of the mediastinum; bronchus intermedius and left lower lobe bronchus visible as paired lucencies.
frames.notes: Fourth frame supplied, caudal to the main-bronchi frame. First frame in this study on which the lower lobes are substantially in view. Pixels not attached.

frames.slice_level: Lower thorax approaching the lung bases, approximately T8-T9. Heart occupies the central mediastinum; both lower lobes broadly in view.
frames.notes: Fifth frame supplied, caudal to the heart-level frame. This frame resolves the question left open on frame 4: the right lower lobe abnormality is extensive and structural, not crowded vasculature. Pixels not attached.

frames.slice_level: Lung bases approaching the diaphragm, approximately T9-T10. Lung cross-sections reducing; central soft tissue is heart with diaphragm and upper abdominal contents beginning to enter the field.
frames.notes: Sixth frame supplied, the most caudal so far. Shows the basal process to be bilateral rather than confined to the right, with a posterior and dependent predominance on both sides. Pixels not attached.

findings.description: Diffuse interlobular septal thickening. Seen on the screenshot frames as coarse irregular reticular and branching lines in both lower lobes and attributed there to a chronic fibrotic or airway background; the official report identifies it as septal thickening, a component of interstitial pulmonary edema.

Peribronchial wall thickening. Seen on the screenshot frames as small rounded and tubular air-density lucencies within opacity and read there as dilated airways, which put bronchiectasis at the head of the differential. They are cuffed normal bronchi, not dilated ones. This single misreading is the hinge on which the whole screenshot interpretation turned.

Perihilar ground-glass opacity and consolidation. The screenshot read described opacity 'extending from the perihilar region laterally and posteriorly' without recognising the perihilar distribution as the signature of edema, and could not identify ground-glass at all on a soft-tissue window.

Pulmonary edema, the unifying diagnosis for the septal thickening, peribronchial wall thickening, and perihilar ground-glass and consolidation above. Not reached by the screenshot read, which proposed bronchiectasis, aspiration or bronchopneumonia, and tree-in-bud bronchiolitis instead.

findings.location: peripheral, both lungs, slight upper lobe predominance
findings.description: Multiple bilateral peripheral nodules with slight upper lobe predominance, explicitly noted as not typical in appearance for edema — a second process alongside it. Suspicion of a ground-glass halo around several, which the report cautions may be exaggerated by motion artefact. No cavitary lesion. Entirely missed by the screenshot read, which called the three upper-thorax frames unremarkable.
9 mm left upper lobe nodule, cited in the official report as an example of the peripheral nodules. Size is the reported measurement from the full study, not a screenshot estimate.
9 mm right upper lobe nodule, cited in the official report as an example of the peripheral nodules. Size is the reported measurement from the full study, not a screenshot estimate.

impression: Pulmonary edema — diffuse interlobular septal thickening, peribronchial wall thickening, and perihilar ground-glass and consolidation — with a second, separate process superimposed: multiple bilateral peripheral nodules with slight upper lobe predominance, explicitly not typical for edema, including a 9 mm left upper lobe nodule and a 9 mm right upper lobe nodule. Suspicion of a ground-glass halo around several of the nodules, possibly exaggerated by motion artefact. No cavitary lesion. This impression follows the official report, which supersedes the screenshot-derived read recorded across the six supplied frames. That read identified the septal thickening, the peribronchial changes, and the perihilar opacity but attributed all three to airway disease — bronchiectasis, aspiration, and bronchiolitis — and did not reach edema. It also called the three upper-thorax frames unremarkable and missed the nodules entirely. See official_report.read_delta for the full account of what held up and what did not.

limitations: Confidence is high because this case carries the official report, not because the screenshots supported it. The screenshot-derived read reached the wrong pattern and missed the nodules; nothing about the frames themselves became more informative.

The nature of the peripheral nodules is unresolved. The report describes them and declines to commit to an entity; this record does the same. Halo, upper lobe predominance, and absence of cavitation are recorded as described, not interpreted.
The ground-glass halo is reported as suspected and possibly exaggerated by motion artefact. It should not be treated as an established feature.
The named nodules sit at report images 83 and 96. Neither slice was among the six frames supplied, so no screenshot in this record shows them and seen_on is empty for those findings.
The 9 mm measurements come from the official report, read off the full study. They are not screenshot estimates and should not be re-derived from any frame here.

Six axial soft-tissue-window frames were supplied, spanning roughly T2 to T10. Ground-glass, septal detail, and small peripheral nodules are all lung-window findings; this window could not have characterised any of them, and the record said so on every frame.

No clinical context supplied — no age, sex, symptoms, cardiac or renal history, immune status, or fluid balance. Edema has causes, and the nodules have a differential that turns almost entirely on immune status and history.
Non-contrast, and no DICOM metadata. Study date unknown.
Single acquisition, confirmed by the user. No prior and no follow-up in the base, so nothing establishes whether the edema or the nodules are new, resolving, or progressing.
notes: First case in the base, and the most instructive one in it. Carries an official report that supersedes the screenshot-derived read. The screenshot read recharacterised three real features as airway disease and missed both the unifying diagnosis of edema and a separate nodular process. Superseded finding slugs, retired when the report arrived: 'rll-posteromedial-opacity' (frame 4, possible certainty, attributed to crowded vasculature), 'rll-heterogeneous-opacity' and 'lll-nodular-opacity' (frames 5-6, attributed to bronchiectasis or aspiration). No comparison had been run against any of them, so no comparison history was broken. Image pixels not attached for any frame — all six screenshots arrived as conversation attachments rather than files.

official_report.text: There is diffuse interlobular septal thickening, peribronchial wall thickening, and perihilar ground-glass and consolidation in keeping with pulmonary edema. However, there are additional bilateral peripheral nodules in both lungs with a slight upper lobe predominance, not typical in appearance for edema. For example, these include 9 mm nodule in the left upper lobe (image 83) and 9 mm nodule in the right upper lobe (image 96). There is suspicion for a ground-glass halo around several of the lesions, although this may be exaggerated by motion artifact. No cavitary lesion.
official_report.read_delta:
The screenshot read got the pattern wrong and missed the nodules entirely.

RECHARACTERISED — the basal abnormality is pulmonary edema, not airway disease. Every component was seen and every component was misattributed. The 'coarse irregular reticular and branching lines' are interlobular septal thickening. The 'small rounded and tubular air-density lucencies' are peribronchial cuffing around normal air-filled bronchi, not dilated airways; that single misreading drove bronchiectasis to the top of the differential and kept it there across two frames. The 'irregular opacity extending from the perihilar region' is perihilar ground-glass and consolidation — the screenshot read described the perihilar distribution in those words without recognising it as the signature of edema.

MISSED — bilateral peripheral nodules with slight upper lobe predominance, including a 9 mm left upper lobe nodule and a 9 mm right upper lobe nodule, with suspicion of ground-glass halo. The three upper-thorax frames were called 'unremarkable'. The standing limitation that a soft-tissue window cannot assess for nodules was recorded correctly on every frame, but the impression used the word 'unremarkable' anyway, which is stronger than the limitation permits. A 9 mm peripheral nodule on soft-tissue window is close to invisible, and the named nodules sit at image 83 and 96, slices that were never supplied — so this was not necessarily findable here. That explains the miss; it does not excuse the wording.

OVER-CALLED — nothing in the differential's leading positions survives. Bronchiectasis with mucus plugging, aspiration or bronchopneumonia, and tree-in-bud bronchiolitis were all ranked moderate and all are wrong. Fibrosis was correctly ranked low. Dependent atelectasis and partial volume were correctly rejected.

WHAT HELD UP — the abnormality was correctly called definitely present, correctly called bilateral and right greater than left, correctly called not vascular, and correctly escalated as significant and needing review of the actual study. No size or attenuation was ever invented. The structural discipline held; the interpretation did not.
